what: A recorded hand-check of PubTator 3.0 relations loaded as 'treats vitiligo', so the dataset card's figure traces to a sample someone else can re-judge.
why: The card stated '30 of 34 treats vitiligo' and '31 of 34 gene associated with vitiligo' from a 2026 check whose sample was never recorded, so neither figure could be reproduced. Both are withdrawn; this file replaces the first of them.

method.population: graph_edges with extraction_method 'pubtator3', predicate TREATS, object 'Vitiligo' (203 relations on 2026-11-23)
method.sample: 10 of a random sample of 34 drawn with Python random.Random(20261123).sample over the relations ordered by edge id
method.judged_on: the single evidence row with the highest PubTator score, read as the paper's title and abstract in the local corpus
method.verdict_rule: supported = that paper states the drug treats, repigments or is therapeutic in vitiligo; not_supported = it does not, whatever other papers on the relation may say
method.caveat: Each relation carries 1 to 33 papers. Judging only the strongest one undercounts: a relation whose top paper does not support it may be supported by another. Read this as a floor on correctness, not as a rate.

rows.reason: Oxidopamine is the agent that depletes the nerves in the model, and the result was null. No sentence names it with vitiligo.

PubTator 3.0 also reads registry records. Its strongest row here restates a trial, so this relation cannot be judged as a reading of a paper.
